summary: The nine example rows of the Search Syntax table take a click. `search_help` in src/finder/dialogs.rs builds the rows inside the dialog's builder now (the `ROWS` const is gone; each entry has a third field that says whether it is an example), gives every row the id ("syntax-row", ix), an aria_label and test_support, and gives the examples a pointer cursor, a hover background, aria_selected and an on_click. The click calls the new private `Finder::search_for_example`: Contents off, the example into the search field with single spaces, and `set_query(.., true, ..)` so it is searched for at once. The dialog stays open and marks the row whose example equals the current name search (theme.primary.opacity(0.14)), whitespace ignored. The first row's text follows config.search.typos, the footer starts with "Click an example to try it.", the dialog is 580 wide instead of 560 and rows have 6 px at each side. All source changes are in src/finder/dialogs.rs; mod.rs is untouched. Review changed two things in the code. The field is edited with InputState::replace_all instead of set_value, so the field's undo history survives and Undo in the search field brings back what an example replaced. And a row acts only on a click whose click_count is 1: in a small window the dialog opens over the (i) that was clicked for it, and the second click of a double-click on the (i) landed on a row and replaced the search.
changelog: Click an example in the Search Syntax table (Cmd+/) to try it. The example goes into the search field in place of what was there and is searched for right away, by name even if Contents was on. Undo in the search field (Cmd+Z) brings back what it replaced. The table stays open so you can try one after another, and it highlights the row of the example that's being searched for. Its first row now says whether typos are allowed, as **Allow typos** is set; it used to read "typos allowed in Settings" either way.
behaviour_changes: In the Search Syntax dialog (Cmd+/, the (i) in the scope bar, Actions > Search Syntax…, Edit > Search Syntax…), a click on any of the nine example rows replaces the search field's text with the example, written with single spaces, and searches for it at once, without the 50 ms a typed search waits. The dialog stays open. This works from a folder (it starts a search) and during a search (it replaces the words).
A click on an example turns Contents off, so the search is by name. Kind, scope and a Nushell filter are left as set.

Undo in the search field (Cmd+Z with the keyboard there, or Edit > Undo) brings back what the example replaced: one step per example tried, then the words typed before. A click on the example that is already in the field adds no step. Undo brings back the words only; Contents stays off. With the keyboard in the files, Cmd+Z is the files' Undo as before and doesn't touch the search.

The row whose example equals the current name search has the accent-tinted background. Whitespace differences are ignored. It applies whether the example was clicked or typed, and when the dialog is opened again during that search. During a Contents search no row is marked, also when the words are an example's.
Example rows show a pointer cursor, and a hover background when not marked. The "Kind menu" and "Contents" rows do nothing on click and have no hover or pointer.

A double-click on an example is the same as one click: nothing is opened and the window does not navigate. A row ignores a click that the system counts as the second or later in a row at that spot. So a double-click on the (i), or on a menu's Search Syntax… item, whose second click lands on a row that the dialog put under the pointer leaves the search alone. (Without that, in a window 700 by 420 or 640 by 400 the double-click replaced "atlas" with an example; seen in review.)
First row text: "Fuzzy words; every word must match (typos allowed)" with Allow typos on, "… (typos off in Settings)" with it off. It was "… (typos allowed in Settings)" in both cases.
The muted footer now starts with "Click an example to try it."
The dialog is 580 wide instead of 560. Every row has 6 px of padding at its sides, so the table's text sits 6 px in from the title and footer, and rows have rounded corners.

Closing works as before (Done, Return, Escape, the ×, the backdrop); Done, Return and Escape were tried after a click on a row. The keyboard returns where it was: the files, the search field with the caret after the example, or in split view the files of the pane whose (i) was clicked.
docs/manual.md: the paragraph under the Search syntax table describes the above, Undo included.
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.
README.md line 116 ("Cmd+/ shows the full syntax in the app.") is still true and was left.
Keyboard access to the rows: they have no tab stop and no role, so an example can only be tried with the mouse. Not in the brief.

The "Kind menu" and "Contents" rows keep the look of the examples (blue, monospaced) though they take no click; only the missing hover and pointer tell them apart. The brief asks for nine clickable rows and no restyling.
Undo does not turn Contents back on, and nothing restores the replaced words while the keyboard is in the files (Cmd+Z there is the files' Undo).

No kept test for the hover background, the highlight's colour, the layout, or the pointer cursor. All but the cursor, which no picture shows, were looked at in pictures: light and dark, at 1100x700, at 640x420 and at Text size 1.3.

No kept test drives the real double-click on the (i) in a small window: where the (i) ends up under the dialog depends on the fonts. The kept test sends the lone second click to a row (Ui::second_click, new in tests/common/mod.rs); the real double-click was probed at six window sizes with a throwaway test, before and after the fix.
cargo clippy --features term was not run: src/term is untouched and nothing it calls changed.
Not compiled for macOS or Windows. The change has no cfg-specific code.

review_fixes: A double-click on the (i) could replace the search. The dialog stays open so that a double-click on an example is harmless, but nobody had looked at a double-click on what opens the dialog. In a small window the dialog opens over the (i), and the second click lands on the row now under the pointer. Probed with a throwaway test at six window sizes: at 700x420 the query "atlas" became "\"tax exemption\"", at 640x400 it became "*.pdf *.md"; at 900x480, 1100x520, 1100x560 and 1100x700 the second click hit the backdrop and closed the dialog, as it did before this change. Where the (i) is depends on the window's width (the scope bar wraps), on the sidebar, and on split view, whose left pane has its (i) in the middle of the window; I did not map out every size. Fix: the row's listener calls search_for_example only when event.click_count() == 1 (views.rs tests a click's count the same way). A genuine double-click on a row is unchanged: its first click is the one that counts. Kept test: a_double_click_on_what_opens_search_syntax_tries_no_example, with the new harness method Ui::second_click, which sends only the second click of a double-click. After the fix the probe leaves "atlas" at all six sizes, and so does a double-click on the left pane's (i) in split view at 1100x500, where the (i) is under the third row.

The click threw away the search field's undo history. The implementer used set_value, as the plan says; it clears the history, so the words the example replaced were gone for good. That is the first item in the brief's risks, which names replace_all as the way out. search_for_example now edits the field with InputState::replace_all (and only when the field doesn't have the example already). The edit sends InputEvent::Change; on_search_event then calls set_query with the words that are already set, which returns at once, so nothing searches twice. The explicit set_query(.., true, ..) stays, for the search to start with the click and not 50 ms later. Probed before and after: with set_value two presses of Cmd+Z left "!*.log !test"; with replace_all they gave "*.pdf *.md" and then "atlas". Kept test: undo_in_the_search_field_brings_back_what_an_example_replaced. docs/manual.md and the Changelog paragraph say it.

Added search_syntax_marks_no_example_during_a_contents_search. Nothing pinned that a Contents search marks no row, or that a click on the example whose words are already being searched for in files still switches to names (there set_query returns early and set_search_contents does the work).

a_search_syntax_example_takes_the_place_of_a_contents_search now checks the answer before any time has passed. With the field edit sending a change event, the explicit set_query would otherwise have been untested: without it every test passed 50 ms later.
Commit message: the paragraph on set_value rewritten for the undoable edit, a paragraph on the two double-clicks, one sentence on Contents and the highlight, and Undo in the Changelog paragraph.

Rebased three times, onto 9cf7635 (escape-ends-search), 69b956f (history-menus) and 65da066 (kind-filter-single-list), which landed during the review. No conflicts. Read all three: the first adds capture_action listeners for the field's Escape in toolbar.rs and filter.rs, the second reworks go_back and go_forward, the third changes how the engine reads a kind; none touches what search_for_example calls. check.sh was run on each rebased tree.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit 06d84e9: 544 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. Before that it printed CHECK OK on two earlier states of the commit: rebased on 9cf7635, before the click-count guard was added (531 passed), and with everything in it on 69b956f (539 passed). The trunk moved three times during the review. Pushed to origin (65da066..06d84e9).

Tests fail without the change: with the src diff of the implementer's commit reverse-applied, its three tests failed (missing ElementId ("syntax-row", N)) and closing_search_syntax_gives_the_keyboard_back_to_the_search_field passed; the three tests added in review start at a syntax-row too. Then five mutations of the final code, one at a time, each run against the Search Syntax tests in tests/controls.rs: set_value in place of replace_all (only the undo test fails); no set_search_contents(false) (the two Contents tests fail); no explicit set_query (the Contents test fails at the names, which are still empty); the mark computed without !search_contents (the marks-no-example test fails); no click_count guard (the opener test fails). A sixth, replace_all without the `field.value() != query` test, fails nothing: the kit drops an edit that changes nothing (undo_manager.rs, record_transaction), so the test in front of it only spares a change event and leaves the caret where it was.

The implementer's deviation 1 (no window.refresh() in the listener) is right, for a second reason besides the one given: gpui-pre's div calls window.refresh() itself on the mouse-up of any element that has a click listener (elements/div.rs, the MouseUpEvent capture handler), before the listeners run. And the Finder's notify marks the window dirty because the Finder is read during the draw. Deviation 2 (580 wide): kept. With this container's font the longer first-row text needs it; I looked at both texts, in a 640x420 window, and at Text size 1.3.

Probed with throwaway tests, not kept: after a click on a row, Return and Escape still close the dialog and the files or the search field have the keyboard again; a right or middle click on a row does nothing; in a file chooser (--pick) a click and a double-click on a row search and choose nothing, and Return closes the dialog only; in split view the (i) of the other pane searches in that pane and Cmd+/ in the pane that has the keyboard; with Contents left on by a search that ended, a click from a folder searches by name, and Escape afterwards puts the folder back with what was selected. All probes are removed and the lane is clean.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code says. (1) A click takes away what was being searched for, with no way back. It did: set_value cleared the field's history. Fixed with the undoable edit; what stays lost is Contents, which Undo doesn't turn back on, and there is no way back while the keyboard is in the files. (2) A click that was never meant for an example does something: a double-click passing through, or landing on a row. A double-click on a row is harmless because the dialog stays; a double-click on the (i) in a small window was not, and is now. The dialog's surface occludes, and while it leaves, a shield over it stops presses (dialog.rs), so no click reaches a row of a closing dialog. (3) The keyboard ends up nowhere after the dialog closes. It returns to what had it (files, search field, the other pane's files), and Return and Escape work after a row was clicked, because a press inside the dialog only refocuses the dialog's own host.

The notes earlier records left for this brief were heeded. The tests use `*.pdf *.md` with Any Kind, which finds Roadmap.md in the fixture, and assert on the search field's words (folder-filter-any-kind, and kind-filter-single-list, which landed during the review: with a kind chosen the example lists only that kind's files). closing_search_syntax_gives_the_keyboard_back_to_the_search_field passes unchanged (scope-chips-keep-focus). The second search after Contents never runs (search-skeleton-flash). After 9cf7635 (escape-ends-search), Escape in the search field once the dialog has closed empties the field and ends the example's search, and the field's history goes on from there: probed on the trunk commit, Cmd+Z then gave the example back, then "atlas", then the empty field.

For briefs still to come.

- regex-content-search: your optional extra row goes into `rows` inside the dialog's builder in search_help; there is no ROWS const and no array length any more. Each entry has a third field: true makes the row an example that a click searches for. A row about regular expressions must be false, like "Kind menu" and "Contents": a click on an example turns Contents off and searches names, the opposite of what such a row would show. The dialog is 580 wide and the first column 150; a longer text than "Fuzzy words; every word must match (typos off in Settings)" pushes that row's second column to the left. If search_regex becomes search state, search_for_example leaves it as it is; decide whether it should.

- recent-searches: search_for_example in dialogs.rs is one more place that sets the search from code, and on purpose it does not use set_value: it calls replace_all, which keeps the field's undo history and sends InputEvent::Change. Don't fold it into a `search_for` helper built on set_value; undo_in_the_search_field_brings_back_what_an_example_replaced would fail. Your plan resets search_recall in InputEvent::Change, so an example click resets it, which is right. An example is not remembered until Return, Down Arrow or an open, like typed words. If Up recall should be undoable too, replace_all is how.

- back-forward-restore-search: nothing to do. An example starts or replaces a search through set_query, like typing. restore_search with set_value clears the field's history, so Undo in the field won't reach back past a Back; that is as it was.

- smart-folder-save-and-leaks: search_for_example calls set_search_contents(false, cx) also outside a search, for Contents left on by a search that ended (probed). If you turn Contents off when a search ends, the call stays right and that case goes away. Three tests here click by-contents during a search.

- search-settings-hints-steppers, typo-fallback-near-miss: the dialog's first row reads "(typos allowed)" or "(typos off in Settings)" from config.search.typos, search_syntax_says_whether_typos_are_allowed compares both labels whole, and the last sentence of the manual paragraph under the syntax table names **Allow typos**. If you rename the switch or change what it means, change those three with it.

- empty-state-messages, search-start-no-flash, live-search-results: after Contents, search_for_example calls run_search twice in one go (set_search_contents, then set_query). The first task is dropped before it is polled, so one search runs. a_search_syntax_example_takes_the_place_of_a_contents_search expects the example's answer with no time passing (click_without_settling, then run_until_parked). An example often ends in No Results; the manual says so now.

- multi-word-highlights, query-history-boost, result-tie-break, sorted-search-results, scoped-search-special-folder-names: the paragraph under the syntax table in docs/manual.md ("Cmd+/ shows this table in the app. …") is one long line now. Edits to the table's rows or to the paragraphs after it don't collide with it. The tests here expect one result or sort the names, so another order of results doesn't touch them.

- focus-lost-recovery, split-active-pane: the tests here expect the keyboard back in the files or the search field after the dialog closes, and in split view in the files of the pane whose (i) was clicked (probed, no kept test).

- Anyone who needs the lone second click of a double-click in a test: Ui::second_click(id) in tests/common/mod.rs. click_point there now goes through click_point_as, which takes the click's count.

Found, not fixed (all there before this change).

- A double-click on a dialog's Done button opens the file under it. The first click closes the dialog and the second lands on the file list as the second click of a double-click. Probed with 60 files in the list view: Cmd+/, then a double-click on Done, gave Open("…/file-18.txt") and that file selected. Only Done was probed; by the same path it should hold for any button that closes a dialog over the files (Cancel, the ×) and for the backdrop. One way to cover them all would be a guard in item_interactions (views.rs) against a second click whose first one went elsewhere.

- A double-click on the (i) in a window where the dialog doesn't open over it (most sizes) opens the Search Syntax dialog and closes it again, because the second click lands on the backdrop. Seen at 1100x700, 1100x560, 1100x520 and 900x480.

- check.sh never compiles the app the way it ships. cargo clippy --all-targets and cargo test both turn on gpui-kit's test-support feature through the dev-dependency, so `.test_support()` always returns the observed wrapper there; code that only compiles with it would print CHECK OK and fail `cargo build`. For this change I also built the library plainly (cargo build -j2 --lib on the final tree): it compiles without warnings. That took 28 s only because lane-g already had a plain build of the dependencies from the morning; in a lane without one it would compile every dependency a second time, so it belongs in the final pass, once, not in every lane.

Not verifiable here: the look with the macOS and Windows fonts (the 580 width was chosen for this container's wide font), the pointer cursor, and the macOS and Windows builds.
